rationale: All three lenses ran (blind, edge-case, acceptance); acceptance audited the full 10-criteria spec and all 10 pass. One blocking finding survived triage: the multiprocessing datasource path (_load_docs_parallel) still swallows the new UnreadableWorkbookError via a bare `except Exception`, so item 5's requirement that BOTH serial and parallel paths account a corrupt xlsb as failed (not silently dropped) is only met on the serial path. Dismissed as non-blocking: the propagate-and-abort behavior on the serial path (intentional per AC6), .xlsm->.xlsx ext coercion (no engine-selection change — XlsxProcessor only branches on .xlsb), the latent **kwargs->Exception.__init__ forward (matches existing SkippedFileException style, no caller passes kwargs), the unregistered/dead-code XlsxConverter (explicitly accepted PO decision in item 2), and one lenient test-only assertion in the skipped e2e scaffold.

Item 7: e2e fixture scaffold + README committed; skips cleanly

No secrets, injection, or unsafe file/process handling; new exception carries only filename + engine error string.

findings.problem: _load_docs_parallel's bare `except Exception as e: logger.error(...)` catches the propagated UnreadableWorkbookError and continues without re-raising or incrementing any stats counter. When ENABLE_FILE_MULTIPROCESSING is true, a corrupt/encrypted xlsb is logged but the job still produces the generic NoChunksImportedException (if it was the only file) or silently omits the file among valid ones — exactly the behavior item 5 set out to eliminate. The serial path (_lazy_load_documents) propagates the typed exception, so the two ingestion paths are inconsistent.
findings.impact: With multiprocessing enabled, ingesting a single corrupt report.xlsb yields the generic NoChunksImportedException instead of the actionable UnreadableWorkbookError message (AC6); a corrupt file among valid ones is dropped with only a log line.
findings.recommendation: In _load_docs_parallel, catch UnreadableWorkbookError before the generic `except Exception` and re-raise it (propagate), matching _lazy_load_documents. Add a test asserting the parallel path propagates it.
